clinical.citation: Vinpocetine improved neuropsychiatric and epileptic outcomes in a patient with a GABRA1 loss-of-function variant (PMID: 37434477)

phenotypes: seizure freedom and improved quality of life on vinpocetine 40 mg daily

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Described as a loss-of-function GABRA1 variant (functionally characterized); the patient had epilepsy with autism and psychiatric comorbidity

clinical.citation: Epi4K Consortium et al. 2013 - De novo mutations in epileptic encephalopathies (PMID: 23934111)

variants.description: not specified in abstract (de novo GABRA1 variant)
phenotypes: infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (epileptic encephalopathy)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo mutation confirmed by trio exome sequencing in a gene intolerant to variation

clinical.citation: Use of a Dynamic Genetic Testing Approach for Childhood-Onset Epilepsy (PMID: 30977854)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Diagnostic finding on the exome-based 100-gene epilepsy panel

clinical.citation: Novel and de novo mutations in pediatric refractory epilepsy (PMID: 30185235)

variants.description: not specified in abstract (novel GABRA1 variant)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Novel pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant classified by ACMG criteria

clinical.citation: ASHG 2017 - Discovery of cerebral palsy genes through trio-based whole exome sequencing in cryptogenic individuals
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Putatively damaging variant identified by trio whole exome sequencing in a gene linked to autism and intellectual disability
clinical.center_country: USA/Australia (Yale, Univ. of Adelaide, Barrow Neurological Institute)

model_organism.citation: Epilepsy plus blindness in microdeletion of GABRA1 and GABRG2 in mouse and human (PMID: 37703949)
phenotypes: reduced GABAA receptor α1, β2 and γ2 subunit expression in various brain regions
optic nerve degeneration with increased G-ratio, indicating impaired myelination
phenobarbital was the most effective anticonvulsant
the human patient with the same microdeletion has intractable epilepsy and optic atrophy

model_organism.citation: Abnormal expression of GABA(A) receptor subunits and hypomotility upon loss of gabra1 in zebrafish (PMID: 32205311)
phenotypes: abnormal expression of other GABAAR subunits
gabra1 expression restricted to the nervous system
hypomotility partially rescued by human GABRA1 but not by the c.875C>T variant

model_organism.citation: Characterization of the zebrafish gabra1(sa43718/sa43718) germline loss of function allele confirms a function for Gabra1 in motility and nervous system development (PMID: 36747751)
phenotypes: decreased gabra2, gabra3 and gabra5 mRNA
continued response to PTZ, indicating residual GABAAR
proteomics showed abnormal expression of proteins for proton transport, ion homeostasis, vesicle transport and mitochondrial complexes

model_organism.citation: Characterization of the zebrafish gabra1(sa43718/sa43718) germline loss of function allele confirms a function for Gabra1 in motility and nervous system development (PMID: 38908344)
phenotypes: decreased gabra2, gabra3 and gabra5 mRNA
proteomics showed abnormal synaptic vesicle fusion, vesicle transport, synapse development and mitochondrial complex proteins

model_organism.citation: Single and Synergistic Effects of Cannabidiol and Δ-9-Tetrahydrocannabinol on Zebrafish Models of Neuro-Hyperactivity (PMID: 30949046)
phenotypes: CBD and THC reduced the hyperactivity
each cannabinoid alone was less effective in the mutant than in the PTZ model

model_organism.citation: Differential role of GABA(A) receptors and neuroligin 2 for perisomatic GABAergic synapse formation in the hippocampus (PMID: 28643105)
phenotypes: absence of α1-GABAAR increased GABAergic synapses containing the α2 subunit
distinct roles for α1- and α2-GABAARs in GABAergic circuit formation

model_organism.citation: A brain-to-gut signal controls intestinal fat absorption (PMID: 39261733)
phenotypes: Gabra1 knockout in the dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV)
largely abolished puerarin-induced intestinal fat loss
puerarin binds GABRA1 to suppress the DMV-vagus-jejunum axis, shortening microvilli and reducing fat absorption

model_organism.citation: A Zebrafish-Based Platform for High-Throughput Epilepsy Modeling and Drug Screening in F0 (PMID: 38474238)
phenotypes: multiparametric behavioral analysis after an epileptogenic stimulus
seizure-like events identified from kinematic parameters
gabra1 and scn1a have the strongest association with photosensitivity

model_organism.citation: Dynamics of sensorimotor cortex activation during absence and myoclonic seizures in a mouse model of juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (PMID: 27573707)
phenotypes: increased EEG connectivity at seizure onset
myoclonic seizure spikes started more focally and had higher voltage than SWD spikes

biological.citation: Understanding paralogous epilepsy-associated GABA(A) receptor variants: Clinical implications, mechanisms, and potential pitfalls (PMID: 39642202)
biological.summary: The α1 P260L and P260S variants in the conserved M1 proline of GABRA1 were studied electrophysiologically in α1β2/3γ2 receptors and by molecular dynamics. They increased GABA sensitivity 3- to 23-fold (gain of function), sometimes with reduced maximal current and enhanced desensitization. Effects depended on which subunit was mutated and on how many subunits carried the mutation.

biological.citation: Improving Proteostasis of Trafficking-Deficient GABA(A) Receptor Variants by Activating IRE1 (PMID: 41178115)
biological.summary: The GABRA1 variants D219N, G251D and P260L are trafficking-deficient. IRE1/XBP1s activation (IXA62, IXA554, IXA105) raised total and surface protein of the variants in HEK293T cells without changing wild-type levels. It also increased GABA-evoked currents for D219N and G251D, and remodeled the proteostasis network in HEK293T cells and in iPSC-derived neurons carrying α1(G251D).

biological.citation: Phenotypic spectrum of GABRA1: From generalized epilepsies to severe epileptic encephalopathies (PMID: 27521439)
biological.summary: In a cohort of 16 novel probands plus 3 family members with GABRA1 mutations, phenotypes ranged from mild generalized epilepsies to severe epileptic encephalopathy. Four mutations tested in Xenopus oocytes showed loss of function.
biological.sample_size: 16 probands + 3 relatives; 4 mutations tested in oocytes

biological.citation: Inhibition of microRNA-129-2-3p protects against refractory temporal lobe epilepsy by regulating GABRA1 (PMID: 34029007)
biological.summary: GABRA1 is a direct target of miR-129-2-3p, shown by luciferase assay on the 3'UTR. In kainic acid-treated rat hippocampal neurons and the KA seizure model, miR-129-2-3p rose while GABRA1 mRNA and protein fell. Antagomir knockdown restored GABRA1 and reduced seizure-like EEG activity, partly in a GABRA1-dependent manner.

biological.citation: Mir-139-5p inhibits glioma cell proliferation and progression by targeting GABRA1 (PMID: 34001135)
biological.summary: GABRA1 is a functional downstream target of miR-139-5p in glioma. GABRA1 knockdown mimicked the miR-139-5p overexpression phenotype of reduced proliferation, migration and invasion. GABRA1 upregulation rescued these effects.
biological.sample_size: GEO datasets GSE90603/GSE90598; 59 DEMs, 419 DEGs, 129 overlapping genes

biological.citation: Distinct Functional Alterations and Therapeutic Options of Two Pathological De Novo Variants of the T292 Residue of GABRA1 (PMID: 35269865)
biological.summary: In HEK293 cells, α1 T292S increased GABA-evoked currents and channel open time (gain of function), while T292I reduced currents and open probability (loss of function). Thiocolchicoside normalized T292S, and diazepam plus verapamil largely rescued T292I. T292 is a critical residue for channel gating.

biological.citation: Abnormal expression of GABA(A) receptor subunits and hypomotility upon loss of gabra1 in zebrafish (PMID: 32205311)
biological.summary: Zebrafish gabra1 expression is restricted to the nervous system. Morpholino knockdown caused hypoactivity and altered expression of other GABAAR subunits. Human GABRA1 partially rescued the hypomotility, whereas the de novo c.875C>T variant did not.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Dissecting heterogeneity of neurodevelopmental disorders using seed centric genetic modules
biological.summary: A network module seeded on GABRA1, built from protein-protein interaction and co-expression data, was associated with long-term potentiation, synaptic vesicle cycle and calcium signaling pathways. Modules were enriched for de novo non-synonymous mutations in epilepsy and other neurodevelopmental cohorts.

biological.citation: ASHG 2009 - Novel mutations found by resequencing multiple subunits of GABA A receptor in families with Idiopathic Generalized Epilepsy
biological.summary: The GABRA1 D219N mutation and the P351fsintX intron-retention insertion were found in IGE families. In transfected mammalian cells the mutant receptors showed reduced cell-surface expression, and D219N had altered gating properties.

biological.citation: A brain-to-gut signal controls intestinal fat absorption (PMID: 39261733)
biological.summary: Cryo-EM and photoaffinity labeling showed that puerarin binds an allosteric modulatory site on the GABAA receptor (GABRA1-containing). Conditional Gabra1 knockout in the DMV largely abolished puerarin-induced intestinal fat loss. This links GABRA1 to brain-to-gut control of fat absorption.
